content.title: About
content.content: Frito pie is a layered dish made with tortilla chips, chili‑seasoned beans, shredded cheese, sour cream, and often ground beef or other meat. It is popular in the American Southwest, especially Texas, where it is commonly served in a paper tray as a “pie.”

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name comes from the Fritos brand corn chips that are traditionally used as the base.
Frito pie is a staple in school cafeterias and sports events because it is quick, hearty, and easy to serve.
There are many variations, including chicken, vegetables, avocado, or vegan cheese alternatives.
In the 1970s the dish gained widespread popularity in Texas thanks to promotional campaigns by fast‑food chains.
It is typically assembled in a single tray, allowing each person to add toppings to taste.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Beans and meat (or plant‑based protein alternatives) provide essential amino acids.

items.title: Good source of fiber
items.content: Beans contain soluble and insoluble fiber that supports digestive health.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are important for blood formation and muscle function.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and beans supply B6 and folate, aiding energy metabolism.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Shredded cheese adds calcium, which helps build strong bones and teeth.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Cheese, sauces, and processed chips can be very salty, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Calorie dense
items.content: The combination of cheese, meat, and chips makes the dish high in calories; portion control is advised.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: Trans‑fat presence
items.content: Some commercial chips contain partially hydrogenated oils.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve Frito pie hot in its paper tray. Start with a layer of chips, then add beans, meat, cheese, sour cream, and any extra toppings (guacamole, onions, tomatoes). Mix before eating so each bite is coated with the flavors.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared Frito pie is best eaten immediately. Leftover components (beans, meat, cheese) should be kept in airtight containers in the refrigerator for 3‑4 days. Store chips dry in a sealed bag to keep them crunchy.
